library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Alihodzic_2022_ciprofloxacin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Alihodzic_2022_ciprofloxacin"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics14050965>

Alihodzic 2022 characterised intravenous ciprofloxacin in critically ill adults
on extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) and used the model to compute the
probability of target attainment (PTA) for an AUC0-24/MIC of at least
125 mg h/L. The structural model has two compartments with first-order
elimination. Plasma bicarbonate and the CKD-EPI estimated glomerular filtration
rate (eGFR, computed with the patient's actual body surface area) both enter
clearance as linear centred effects (Equation 1):

`CL = CLtyp * (1 + 0.0571 * (BICARB - 25.7)) * (1 + 0.0038 * (eGFR - 40.83))`

No ECMO-related variable (cannulation, blood and gas flow, pump speed,
duration) was retained.

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Alihodzic_2022_ciprofloxacin")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
```

# Population

Seventeen adults (16 men, 1 woman) on veno-arterial (8), veno-venous (8) or
veno-veno-arterial (1) ECMO at the University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf,
recruited July 2016 to February 2018 (Alihodzic 2022 Table 1). Median age was
57 years (25-73) and median weight 90 kg (66-123). They were severely ill
(median SOFA 13, SAPS II 48, APACHE II 32), and 12 of the 17 died. Median CKD-EPI
eGFR was 46.8 mL/min (10.7-143) and median plasma bicarbonate 26.6 mmol/L
(18.0-39.0). Twelve patients received 400 mg every 8 h and five 400 mg every
12 h, each as a 30-min infusion. Peak (1 h after the end of infusion), mid-dose
(4 h after) and trough samples were drawn on three days within a 7-day window,
giving 139 analysed plasma samples.

```{r population}
str(ui$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` entry carries an in-file comment naming its origin in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Alihodzic_2022_ciprofloxacin.R`.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Two-compartment model, first-order elimination, IV infusion into central | -- | Results 3.2; Methods 2.3 (30-min infusions) |
| `lcl` (CL at bicarbonate 25.7 mmol/L, eGFR 40.83 mL/min) | 12.9 L/h | Table 2 final model, row `CL (L/h)`; Results 3.2 |
| `lvc` (V1) | 73.4 L | Table 2, row `V 1 (L)` |
| `lq` (Q) | 38.8 L/h | Table 2, row `Q (L/h)` |
| `lvp` (V2) | 87.6 L | Table 2, row `V 2 (L)` |
| `e_bicarbonate_cl` | 0.0571 per mmol/L | Table 2, row `COV_CL_BICARB`; Equation 1 |
| `e_crcl_cl` | 0.0038 per mL/min | Table 2, row `COV_CL_eGFR`; Equation 1 |
| Covariate centring 25.7 mmol/L and 40.83 mL/min | -- | Equation 1; Results 3.2 |
| `etalcl` | 25.8% CV, omega^2 0.0644 | Table 2, row `IIV CL`; footnote `%CV = sqrt(exp(OMEGA) - 1) x 100` |
| `etalvc` | 53.9% CV, omega^2 0.2550 | Table 2, row `IIV V 1` |
| `etalq` | 34.1% CV, omega^2 0.1100 | Table 2, row `IIV Q` |
| No IIV on V2 | -- | Results 3.2 (tended to zero); Table 2 final model `-` |
| `etaiov_cl_1` ... `etaiov_cl_21` | 17.2% CV, omega^2 0.0292 | Table 2, row `IOV CL`; Results 3.2 'each administration was defined as a new occasion' |
| `propSd` | 0.121 | Table 2, row `Prop. sigma (CV%)` 12.1 |

# Deterministic checks

The typical clearance at the centring values and the total volume of
distribution are fixed by the parameter table, so they are asserted exactly.
The Discussion reports a total Vd (V1 + V2) of 161 L.

```{r deterministic}
th <- ui$theta
cl_typ <- function(bic, gfr) {
  exp(th[["lcl"]]) * (1 + th[["e_bicarbonate_cl"]] * (bic - 25.7)) *
    (1 + th[["e_crcl_cl"]] * (gfr - 40.83))
}
vss <- exp(th[["lvc"]]) + exp(th[["lvp"]])
stopifnot(
  abs(cl_typ(25.7, 40.83) - 12.9) < 1e-9,
  abs(vss - 161) < 0.5
)
tibble::tibble(
  scenario = c(
    "Reference (25.7 mmol/L, 40.83 mL/min)", "Bicarbonate 18 mmol/L",
    "Bicarbonate 39 mmol/L", "eGFR 10 mL/min", "eGFR 150 mL/min"
  ),
  bic = c(25.7, 18, 39, 25.7, 25.7),
  gfr = c(40.83, 40.83, 40.83, 10, 150)
) |>
  mutate(cl = cl_typ(bic, gfr)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Scenario" = scenario, "Bicarbonate (mmol/L)" = bic,
    "eGFR (mL/min)" = gfr, "Typical CL (L/h)" = cl
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

# Virtual cohort and comparison with the observed concentrations

The cohort below reproduces the study's covariate spread: bicarbonate and eGFR
are drawn log-normally to match the Table 1 medians and interquartile ranges,
truncated to the observed ranges, and patients are split between the 8- and
12-hourly regimens in roughly the study's 12:5 ratio. Each administration is
its own occasion. Samples are taken at the study's peak, mid-dose and trough
times in the first dosing interval of days 1, 4 and 7, the sampling window of
Methods 2.4.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2022)
n_q8 <- 140
n_q12 <- 60
rtrunc_lnorm <- function(n, med, q1, q3, lo, hi) {
  sdlog <- (log(q3) - log(q1)) / (2 * qnorm(0.75))
  x <- exp(rnorm(n * 4, log(med), sdlog))
  x <- x[x >= lo & x <= hi]
  x[seq_len(n)]
}
cohort <- tibble::tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_q8 + n_q12),
  regimen = c(rep("400 mg q8h", n_q8), rep("400 mg q12h", n_q12)),
  tau = c(rep(8, n_q8), rep(12, n_q12)),
  BICARBONATE = rtrunc_lnorm(n_q8 + n_q12, 26.6, 24.3, 29.7, 18, 39),
  CRCL = rtrunc_lnorm(n_q8 + n_q12, 46.8, 25.4, 79.6, 10.7, 143)
)
stopifnot(!anyNA(cohort$BICARBONATE), !anyNA(cohort$CRCL))

make_cohort_events <- function(cohort) {
  doses <- cohort |>
    group_by(id) |>
    reframe(
      time = seq(0, 168 - tau, by = tau), regimen = regimen, tau = tau,
      BICARBONATE = BICARBONATE, CRCL = CRCL
    ) |>
    group_by(id) |>
    mutate(OCC = row_number(), amt = 400, rate = 800, evid = 1L) |>
    ungroup()
  obs <- cohort |>
    tidyr::crossing(day = c(1, 4, 7), type = c("Peak", "Mid-dose", "Trough")) |>
    mutate(
      start = (day - 1) * 24,
      time = start + dplyr::case_when(
        type == "Peak" ~ 1.5, type == "Mid-dose" ~ 4.5, TRUE ~ tau - 1e-6
      ),
      OCC = start / tau + 1, amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L
    ) |>
    select(id, time, regimen, tau, BICARBONATE, CRCL, OCC, amt, rate, evid, type)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    mutate(cmt = "central") |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
ev_cohort <- make_cohort_events(cohort)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(965)
sim_cohort <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, ev_cohort,
  keep = c("regimen", "type"), returnType = "data.frame"
)
```

Table 1 pools all samples (both regimens, any of the sampling days), so the
simulated medians below are pooled the same way. These are a check on the
overall exposure level rather than on any single parameter.

```{r observed-comparison}
obs_tab <- tibble::tibble(
  type = c("Peak", "Mid-dose", "Trough"),
  observed = c(4.55, 2.57, 1.53),
  observed_iqr = c("3.69-5.90", "1.97-3.45", "1.11-2.57")
)
sim_tab <- sim_cohort |>
  filter(!is.na(type)) |>
  group_by(type) |>
  summarise(
    simulated = median(sim),
    simulated_iqr = sprintf("%.2f-%.2f", quantile(sim, 0.25), quantile(sim, 0.75)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
cmp_obs <- inner_join(obs_tab, sim_tab, by = "type") |>
  mutate(ratio = simulated / observed)
stopifnot(nrow(cmp_obs) == 3)
cmp_obs |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Sample" = type, "Observed median (mg/L)" = observed,
    "Observed IQR" = observed_iqr, "Simulated median (mg/L)" = simulated,
    "Simulated IQR" = simulated_iqr, "Simulated / observed" = ratio
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
# A mis-transcribed clearance or volume (a log-scale slip, a swapped V1/V2)
# moves the medians by far more than these bounds allow.
stopifnot(all(cmp_obs$ratio > 0.6 & cmp_obs$ratio < 1.5))
```

The simulated trough median is close to the observed one, while the simulated
peak and mid-dose medians are about 20% below the observed medians. The same
direction shows up in the PTA comparison below, where the simulated exposure
runs slightly under the paper's. The Discussion notes that infusion times were
not precisely documented. A peak recorded nearer to the end of the infusion than
the nominal 1 h would read high against a model that places it at 1 h.

```{r cohort-plot, fig.cap = "Simulated peak, mid-dose and trough concentrations (points) against the Table 1 observed medians (dashed lines)."}
sim_cohort |>
  filter(!is.na(type)) |>
  mutate(type = factor(type, levels = c("Peak", "Mid-dose", "Trough"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(type, sim)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.3, size = 0.8) +
  geom_errorbar(
    data = obs_tab |> mutate(type = factor(type, levels = c("Peak", "Mid-dose", "Trough"))),
    aes(x = type, ymin = observed, ymax = observed), inherit.aes = FALSE,
    linetype = "dashed", colour = "red", width = 0.6
  ) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~regimen) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Ciprofloxacin (mg/L)")
```

# Typical-value profiles

```{r typical, fig.cap = "Typical-value concentrations over the first 48 h of 400 mg every 8 h at the lowest, reference and highest plasma bicarbonate (eGFR 40.83 mL/min)."}
ev_typ <- tidyr::crossing(
  BICARBONATE = c(18, 25.7, 39),
  time = c(seq(0, 48, by = 0.1), seq(0, 40, by = 8))
) |>
  distinct() |>
  mutate(id = as.integer(factor(BICARBONATE)), CRCL = 40.83)
dose_t <- seq(0, 40, by = 8)
ev_typ <- ev_typ |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0) |>
  bind_rows(
    tidyr::crossing(BICARBONATE = c(18, 25.7, 39), time = dose_t) |>
      mutate(
        id = as.integer(factor(BICARBONATE)), CRCL = 40.83,
        evid = 1L, amt = 400, rate = 800
      )
  ) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  mutate(OCC = pmin(floor(time / 8) + 1, 21)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(cmt = "central") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev_typ,
  keep = "BICARBONATE", returnType = "data.frame"
)
ggplot(sim_typ, aes(time, Cc, colour = factor(BICARBONATE))) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Ciprofloxacin (mg/L)", colour = "Bicarbonate\n(mmol/L)")
```

# PKNCA: AUC0-24 and probability of target attainment

Section 2.6 simulated 1000 patients per scenario at the lowest and highest
observed values of each covariate and counted the fraction achieving
AUC0-24/MIC >= 125 mg h/L. The scenarios below use 200 patients each; the
covariate not being varied is held at its centring value. Each patient receives
400 mg every 8 h, and PKNCA computes the AUC over the first 24 h. Because the
model is linear in dose, the 600 mg and 800 mg AUCs of Figure 4 are the 400 mg
AUCs of the same patients scaled by 1.5 and 2.

```{r pta-sim}
n_per <- 200
scen <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario, ~BICARBONATE, ~CRCL,
  "Bicarbonate 18 mmol/L", 18, 40.83,
  "Bicarbonate 39 mmol/L", 39, 40.83,
  "eGFR 10 mL/min", 25.7, 10,
  "eGFR 150 mL/min", 25.7, 150,
  "Bicarbonate 18 + eGFR 10", 18, 10,
  "Bicarbonate 39 + eGFR 150", 39, 150
) |>
  mutate(sid = row_number())
subj <- tidyr::crossing(scen, rep = seq_len(n_per)) |>
  mutate(id = (sid - 1) * n_per + rep)
ev_pta <- bind_rows(
  tidyr::crossing(subj, k = 1:3) |>
    mutate(time = (k - 1) * 8, OCC = k, amt = 400, rate = 800, evid = 1L),
  tidyr::crossing(subj, time = seq(0, 24, by = 0.25)) |>
    mutate(OCC = pmin(floor(time / 8) + 1, 3), amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L)
) |>
  select(id, scenario, time, BICARBONATE, CRCL, OCC, amt, rate, evid) |>
  mutate(cmt = "central") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
rxode2::rxSetSeed(125)
sim_pta <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_pta, keep = "scenario", returnType = "data.frame")

conc_pta <- sim_pta |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, scenario, time, Cc)
dose_pta <- ev_pta |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, scenario, time, amt)
nca_pta <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_pta, Cc ~ time | scenario + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_pta, amt ~ time | scenario + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, auclast = TRUE)
))
auc24 <- as.data.frame(nca_pta$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  select(scenario, id, auc = PPORRES)
stopifnot(nrow(auc24) == nrow(scen) * n_per, !anyNA(auc24$auc))
```

The paper's PTAs are compared with two readings of "AUC0-24". The first is the
AUC over the first 24 h of therapy, from the PKNCA results above. The second is
the steady-state daily AUC, `daily dose / CL`, whose PTA follows in closed form
from the log-normal clearance (IIV plus IOV) at the typical-value clearance of
each scenario.

```{r pta-table}
om <- ui$omega
sd_cl <- sqrt(om["etalcl", "etalcl"] + om["etaiov_cl_1", "etaiov_cl_1"])
pta_ss <- function(dose_daily, bic, gfr, mic) {
  100 * pnorm((log(dose_daily / (125 * mic)) - log(cl_typ(bic, gfr))) / sd_cl)
}
paper <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario, ~dose, ~paper,
  "Bicarbonate 18 mmol/L", 400, 92.8,
  "Bicarbonate 39 mmol/L", 400, 7.3,
  "eGFR 10 mL/min", 400, 71.7,
  "eGFR 150 mL/min", 400, 21.4,
  "Bicarbonate 39 mmol/L", 600, 66.7,
  "Bicarbonate 39 mmol/L", 800, 95.4
)
pta_cmp <- paper |>
  inner_join(scen, by = "scenario") |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    day1 = 100 * mean(auc24$auc[auc24$scenario == scenario] * dose / 400 / 0.5 >= 125),
    ss = pta_ss(3 * dose, BICARBONATE, CRCL, 0.5)
  ) |>
  ungroup()
stopifnot(nrow(pta_cmp) == nrow(paper))
pta_cmp |>
  transmute(
    scenario, regimen = paste(dose, "mg q8h"), paper, day1, ss
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Scenario" = scenario, "Regimen" = regimen,
    "Paper PTA (%)" = paper, "Simulated PTA, first 24 h (%)" = day1,
    "Steady-state PTA, closed form (%)" = ss
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

At the EUCAST breakpoint of 0.5 mg/L the first-24-h reading reproduces the
direction and size of every published covariate and dose effect. It runs
uniformly below the paper, by between under 1 and about 12 percentage points
depending on the scenario. The steady-state reading does not reproduce the paper:
at bicarbonate 39 mmol/L it gives a PTA several-fold higher than the published
7.3%. The paper's AUC0-24 is therefore the first-day AUC. The remaining
uniform shortfall is unexplained; it corresponds to a simulated AUC roughly 5-10%
below the paper's. The parameters were not adjusted to close it.

```{r pta-assert}
# Centre and envelope of the first-24-h comparison. The per-scenario Monte
# Carlo SE at n = 200 is up to 3.5 points, so the envelope has headroom.
stopifnot(
  mean(abs(pta_cmp$day1 - pta_cmp$paper)) < 12,
  all(abs(pta_cmp$day1 - pta_cmp$paper) < 20)
)
# Deterministic: the steady-state reading misses the bicarbonate 39 mmol/L
# result by a wide margin, which is what identifies the first-day AUC.
ss_bic39 <- pta_ss(1200, 39, 40.83, 0.5)
stopifnot(ss_bic39 - 7.3 > 15)
```

## Replicate Figures 3 and 4

```{r fig3, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3 of Alihodzic 2022: PTA for AUC0-24/MIC >= 125 mg h/L with 400 mg every 8 h across MICs, by covariate scenario. Dotted line: EUCAST breakpoint 0.5 mg/L."}
mics <- c(0.06, 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2)
pta_curve <- tidyr::crossing(auc24, mic = mics) |>
  group_by(scenario, mic) |>
  summarise(pta = 100 * mean(auc / mic >= 125), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(pta_curve, aes(mic, pta, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 90, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dotted") +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = mics) +
  labs(x = "MIC (mg/L)", y = "PTA (%)", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 2))
```

The paper states that at an MIC of 1 mg/L or above the PTA is below 1% for
every covariate value in the single-covariate scenarios of Figure 3A-B. It also states that for the combination of high
bicarbonate and high eGFR the PTA falls below 75% at 0.25 mg/L and below 1% at
0.5 mg/L.

```{r fig3-claims}
pta_at <- function(scn, mic_val) {
  v <- pta_curve$pta[pta_curve$scenario == scn & pta_curve$mic == mic_val]
  if (length(v) != 1L) stop("no unique PTA for ", scn, " at MIC ", mic_val)
  v
}
pta_curve |>
  filter(mic %in% c(0.25, 0.5, 1)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = mic, values_from = pta, names_prefix = "MIC ") |>
  dplyr::rename("Scenario" = scenario) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
stopifnot(
  pta_at("Bicarbonate 39 + eGFR 150", 0.25) < 75,
  pta_at("Bicarbonate 39 + eGFR 150", 0.5) < 5,
  max(pta_curve$pta[pta_curve$mic == 1 & !grepl("\\+", pta_curve$scenario)]) < 10
)
```

```{r fig4, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4 of Alihodzic 2022: PTA for 400, 600 and 800 mg every 8 h at the lowest and highest covariate values."}
pta_dose <- tidyr::crossing(
  auc24 |> filter(!grepl("\\+", scenario)),
  dose = c(400, 600, 800), mic = mics
) |>
  group_by(scenario, dose, mic) |>
  summarise(pta = 100 * mean(auc * dose / 400 / mic >= 125), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(pta_dose, aes(mic, pta, colour = factor(dose))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 90, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dotted") +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = mics) +
  facet_wrap(~scenario) +
  labs(x = "MIC (mg/L)", y = "PTA (%)", colour = "Dose q8h (mg)")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Occasion count.** The paper defines every administration as a new occasion
  but does not state how many occasions the analysis data held. The model
  encodes 21, which covers the 7-day sampling window at 8-hourly dosing; all 21
  share the single estimated IOV variance. Records with `OCC` outside 1-21
  carry no IOV.
* **eGFR units.** The retained eGFR is CKD-EPI computed with the patient's
  actual body surface area, so it is in absolute mL/min rather than the usual
  mL/min/1.73 m^2. It is carried in the `CRCL` column. Users must de-index a
  reported eGFR (multiply by BSA / 1.73) before supplying it.
* **Covariate centring.** Equation 1 centres on 25.7 mmol/L and 40.83 mL/min,
  which differ from the Table 1 per-patient medians (26.6 mmol/L, 46.8 mL/min).
  The equation's values are used. They are probably medians over records
  rather than over patients, but the paper does not say.
* **Range of the bicarbonate effect.** The linear bicarbonate term describes
  the alkalotic side of the observed 18-39 mmol/L range only. The Discussion
  notes that the effect of acidosis was not characterised. Clearance reaches
  zero at 8.2 mmol/L, so the model should not be extrapolated far below the
  observed range.
* **Residual error.** Table 2 reports the proportional error as 12.1% CV and
  states that CVs were obtained as `sqrt(exp(OMEGA) - 1)`. The model uses
  `propSd = 0.121`; back-transforming through that formula would give 0.1206,
  which is immaterial.
* **PTA reading.** The paper does not state the AUC0-24 window. The first-24-h
  window reproduces its PTAs, while the steady-state window does not (see the
  table above). The paper's other covariate was presumably held at a fixed
  value in the single-covariate scenarios. The value is not reported, and the
  centring value is used here. Holding it at the Table 1 median instead lowers
  the PTAs a further 1-6 points.
* **Virtual cohort.** Bicarbonate and eGFR are drawn independently as
  log-normals matched to the Table 1 medians and IQRs. The paper does not report
  their correlation or the per-patient sampling days.
